newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria stages Aida opera at communist mausoleum.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria stages Aida opera at communist mausoleum.

text.p: A marble mausoleum that once held the embalmed corpse of Bulgaria's first communist leader Georgi Dimitrov has been turned into an Egyptian pyramid for an open air staging of Giuseppe Verdi's opera Aida this weekend.

A four metre (13-foot) high mask of the pharaoh Tutankhamen weighing almost a tonne has been erected above the communist tomb as part of the preparations for the three performances, which form part of the Sofia Music Weeks festival.
National opera director Plamen Kartalov said the performances would feature bass Nikola Gyuzelev and soprano Maria Belcheva among 800 singers and extras.
The mausoleum has been empty since 1990 when the remains of Dimitrov, founder of Bulgarian communism and its first communist prime minister, were removed and cremated.
In April the building was covered with more than 100 black dalmatian spots as a promotion for the Walt Disney film "101 Dalmatians".
